*Er lässt den Spaten sinken.* Sie hat be:
*He lowers the spade.* She paid. Miriam. I owe her, from before. I was to fetch the little one's music box.

It's down there. Under the altar. The girl too. I didn't want this.
*Hester steht im Kreis. Ihre Augen sind:
*Hester stands in the circle. Her eyes are open, but empty. She hums.*

“... sleep, child, the water watches ...”
*seufzt* Er ist unten im Keller. Halb er: *sighs* He's down in the cellar. Half frozen, keeps talking about a song. I didn't want her to find him. Please only tell someone you trust.
... Sie sind hartnäckig. Na gut. Elias w: ... You're persistent. Very well. Elias was here yesterday and pawned his silver lantern key. A woman bought it the same evening. See for yourself in the ledger.
Ach, die. Liegt seit Wochen in meiner Ma: Oh, that. Been in my coat pocket for weeks. Take it back before Pimm strangles me.
Agnes Crane blickt nicht von dem Grab au: Agnes Crane doesn't look up from the grave. “You've come about Miriam. Everyone comes about Miriam now.”
Agnes schweigt lange. Dann wischt sie Er:
Agnes is silent for a long time. Then she wipes earth from a gravestone.

“Father Ambrose thinks I'm a witch, doesn't he?”
Ah, der feine Herr Ermittler. Jetzt, wo: Ah, the fine mister investigator. Now that the coppers like you, I don't talk to you no more.
Ah, mein Lieblingsermittler. Was kann ic: Ah, my favourite investigator. What can I do?
Akte 47 fehlt. Irgendein Constable hat s: File 47 is missing. Some constable took it and never brought it back. If you find it, I'll put in a good word for you at the precinct.
Akte 47! Wo war sie? ... Bei Price. Natü:
File 47! Where was it? ... With Price. Of course.

Thank you. I won't forget that.
Alle sagen immer, ich war’s. Beim Theate: Everyone always says it was me. At the theatre, at the master's, even at the baker's. I've just got a face that's easy to point at.
Am Kanalhafen, frühmorgens. Da gehen Fra: At the Canal Harbour, early in the morning. Women in grey coats go into Warehouse 7 with candles in their baskets. And they don't come out before sunrise. Creepy, I tell you. Would make a good headline.
Ambrose crosses himself. “I knew it.” He hurries off to the precinct.

Two days later you hear that the constables arrested an old woman in front of the chapel. She had black candles in her bag and said not a word.
Ambrose setzt sich auf die Stufen. „Agne:
Ambrose sits down on the steps. “Agnes ... Walter played the organ here before he went to St. Ebba. Seven candles. Seven years.”

“And I almost had a grieving widow reported. Thank you. Tomorrow morning I'll kneel beside her.”
An das Lied. Und dann an Arme, die mich: The song. And then arms carrying me. I saw the brass buttons, like the constables have. And he hummed along. He knew the song, every note.
An ein Lied. Mehr nicht. Fragen Sie mich: A song. Nothing more. Ask me another time, when my head is clearer.
Archiv. Bitte nichts anfassen, was Sie n: Archive. Please don't touch anything you're not allowed to touch.
Auf Wache, natürlich. In Ashgrove.\n\nRo:
On watch, of course. In Ashgrove.

Rook smiles. His hand twitches towards his breast pocket, as if he wanted to hide something.
Auf der Bettkante sitzt ein kleines Mädc: A little girl sits on the edge of the bed, hardly more than a shimmer. She holds a music box that doesn't play.
Auf einem Regal zwischen den Zahnrädern: On a shelf between the cogwheels stand dozens of star glass vials. In each one a small light drifts, and each sings something different, softly. Behind you the clock ticks towards 3:33.
Aufgebracht? Mir hat so ein Bengel die K: Upset? Some rascal stole my cash box last night! A boy in a coat far too big for him. Kit's his name, always hangs about the east end.
Barnaby blinzelt in die Gaslaterne, als: Barnaby blinks at the gas lantern as if he hadn't seen one in years. “Fresh air! And all because someone listened. I owe you one, snoop.”
Barnaby ist unschuldig. Lassen Sie ihn f: Barnaby is innocent. Let him go.
Barnaby sitzt unschuldig. Ich habe Bewei: Barnaby is innocent. I have proof.
Keep it to yourself for now.
Beim fünften Takt summen andere mit. Sie: At the fifth bar others hum along. Seven women's voices, close behind you. When you turn around, no one is there.
Famous is an exaggeration. Bitter it is. Here, a bottle. Against scratches and against Kettlegate.
Bess Hagan sagt, Ihr Tonikum hat ihren M: Bess Hagan says your tonic poisoned her husband.
Bess starrt auf das Fass hinter sich. Da: Bess stares at the barrel behind her. Then she kicks it over. “Herring from the last heatwave. I didn't want to throw it away.” She laughs until she cries.
Beweis es doch! Wer sagt das? Eine Aussa: Prove it then! Who says so? One statement, pfff. Could be anyone.
Blumen für jemanden daheim? ... Ach, Sie: Flowers for someone at home? ... Oh, you're the investigator. About Elias, isn't it? Poor fellow.
Bram nickt dir zu. Das ist bei ihm so vi: Bram nods at you. For him that's as good as a hug.
Bram nickt einmal. Am nächsten Tag steht: Bram nods once. The next day Finn stands at the North Gate with his bundle, crying. The barrels keep disappearing.
Bram schaut lange auf seine Hände. Dann:
Bram looks at his hands for a long time. Then he goes over to Finn and lays his paw on his shoulder. The boy flinches, then grins.

Bram comes back and sets two packets in wax paper in front of you. “Ox blood. For honest people.”
Bram wischt sich die Hände an der Schürz: Bram wipes his hands on his apron.
Bram zeigt auf die leeren Haken und die: Bram points to the empty hooks and the gap between the barrels. He says three sentences, more than he usually says in a week.
Brannock setzt sich schwer auf einen Amb: Brannock sits down heavily on an anvil.
Brock steckt deine Münzen ein und pfeift: Brock pockets your coins and whistles. The crowd presses against the railing.
Constable Rook. Sie sind der neue Ermitt: Constable Rook. You're the new investigator? Good luck. Nobody believes you here.
Constable Rook. Und der Chor trifft sich: Constable Rook. And the choir meets in Warehouse 7 at the Canal Harbour.
Darf ich die Gästeliste sehen?: May I see the guest list?
Das Auge? Damit haben die Damen vom Chor: The eye? The ladies of the choir of St. Ebba sealed their letters with it, before the chapel burned down. The choir mistress was called Miriam Vey.
Das Holz splittert. Die Melodie bricht m: The wood splinters. The melody breaks off mid-note. Hester takes a deep breath, as if surfacing from deep water, and then sleeps on peacefully.
Das Klopfen? Das war einer von euch. Jun: The knocking? That was one of yours. Young face, blond hair under the helmet. Winked at me and scratched the eye into the bars. The same one who locked me up.
Das Leder ist kalt und gibt unter dem Da: The leather is cold and gives under your thumb like skin. Thin mist seeps from the cut, and somewhere between the pages someone hums.
Das Licht im Glas wird zu Wänden, die Wä: The light in the glass becomes walls, the walls become pipes.
Das Licht springt dir in die Augen. Minu: The light leaps into your eyes. For minutes you see only white stars, and each of them sings. When you can see again, you have cut your hand on the edge.
Das Lied hat mich bei meinem Namen geruf: The song called me by my name, you understand? I just started walking. Into the water. If the song is calling someone else now ...
Das Lächeln bleibt. Nur die Augen werden: The smile stays. Only the eyes turn grey, like smoke behind glass. “What a pity. I liked this face.”
Das Mädchen nickt und ist fort. Nur die: The girl nods and is gone. Only the music box turns once, all by itself.
Das Nebelvieh? Klar. Ich hab's gesehen,:
The fog beast? Sure. I seen it, from the gutter. It only comes where no lantern's burnin'. When the baker came out with his lamp, it howled and went back into the water.

Hold your lantern in its face. And don't let it bite ya, the wounds go cold.
Das Teleskop glüht. In seinem Spiegel, g:
The telescope glows. In its mirror, as big as a cartwheel, hangs the star, so close that you can make out the lights in it: voices, shadows, sleeping children.

Starling lies on the floor, grey and small, the ledger under his arm. Through the open window you hear dogs, and down the hill lanterns sway.

“Do you hear that? That's Price. You can't smash the star without smashing what you saved. And when the sun rises, he's looking for only one man. You.”
Das Wasser unter dem Steg wird schwarz u:
The water under the jetty turns black and still. A figure rises, translucent, with wet hair. It trembles.

“I didn't want to sing. They said I had to sing along, or else ... The woman in grey nodded, and the policeman pushed me.”
Das ist ein schwerer Vorwurf gegen einen: That's a serious accusation against a constable. I need information confirmed by at least two sources. For both: who, and where.
Dein Spiegelbild greift nach dir. Eine e: Your reflection reaches for you. An ice-cold hand closes around your wrist, and when you pull free, white fingerprints remain on your skin.
Deine Hand zögert. Du weißt nicht, was d: Your hand hesitates. You don't know what this music box is and what will happen if you destroy it. First understand what Vey really wants.
Den Spiegel drehen, bis der Stern sich s: Turn the mirror until the star sees itself, and call every light home by name.
Der Ermittler hat den Nebelhund vom Kana: The investigator drove the fog hound away from the canal.
Der Faden glimmt kurz und zeigt einen Ke: The thread glimmers briefly and shows a cellar passage with a loom at the end. Then it's invisible again.
Der Faden wickelt sich um dein Handgelen: The thread winds around your wrist and pulls. Your eyelids grow heavy, and a stern voice says: “Bedtime.”
The dog from the canal won't be coming back.
The cork springs from your fingers. The voice screams, a single high note that stabs your temples. With shaking hands you push it back in. You heard nothing but the scream.
Der Marktwart vom Altmarkt, Grimes, trin:
The market warden of the Old Market, Grimes, drinks here for free. Says it's part of his wages. Old Wick is afraid of his own lanterns. And Father Ambrose sees the choir everywhere.

Kettlegate is getting strange. Stranger than usual.
Der Rand der Scherbe ist bereift. Dein S: The edge of the shard is frosted. Your reflection in it blinks a heartbeat after you.
The rat catcher lures the children away.
Der Rattenfänger sitzt in der Zelle nebe:
The rat catcher sits in the cell next to Thorne's nephew, in case you brought him in too. He doesn't play any more. Nan was here and screamed at me.

In Ashgrove the children keep wandering.
Der Rostbruder starrt dich an und knackt: The Rust Brother stares at you and cracks his grey knuckles.
Der Schmuggler liegt auf den Planken und: The smuggler lies on the planks clutching his ribs. “All right, all right! What do you want?”
Der Souffleur Felix Dunmore. Er bringt d: The prompter Felix Dunmore. He takes the voices through the old gas tunnel into the clock tower.
Der Souffleur Felix Dunmore. Wo er die S: The prompter Felix Dunmore. Where he hides the voices, I don't know.
Der Stand ist leer. Auf dem Pflaster lie: The stall is empty. A single green bottle lies on the cobbles.
Der Ton hört nicht auf. Er wird tiefer,: The tone doesn't stop. It grows deeper, louder, until blood runs from your nose and the cobblestones tremble. Then suddenly it is silent.
Der Ton ist um ein Haar zu hoch. Er reib: The tone is a hair too high. It grates against everything in your head, and for a moment it goes completely quiet in there.
Der Webstuhl ist voller Fäden, und an je: The loom is full of threads, and a breath hangs from each. Upstairs in the house you hear the children sleeping, all in the same rhythm. Behind the loom lies something small, curled up.
Der Zellengang riecht nach Kalk und kalt: The cell corridor smells of lime and cold tea. Behind the bars sit people you brought here yourself. Some look up as you pass.
Der kleine Thomas. Miriam hat ihn bei si: Little Thomas. Miriam took him in when his mother died. He would do anything for her. Anything.
Der silberne Ton ist um ein Haar zu hoch: The silver tone is a hair too high.
Der Öllieferant vom Hafen. Kommt jede Wo: The oil supplier from the harbour. Comes every week, exchanges silver with the old choir crest for coins. Says it's payment for Warehouse 7. None of my business.
Der? Würde mich nicht wundern, wenn der: Him? Wouldn't surprise me if he robs graves. Odd fellow. Lives all alone in the ruins.
The letters to the precinct. That was you.
Die Fäden einzeln durchschneiden und jed: Cut the threads one by one and call each child by name.
Die Gestalt löst sich auf wie Atem im Wi: The figure dissolves like breath in winter. The water turns grey again.
Die Glocke ganz tief in die Tasche steck: Put the bell deep into your pocket.
Die Glocke hängt in der Mitte der Kammer: The bell hangs in the middle of the chamber, black and warm. Faces move in its metal, seven, and their mouths are open. Miriam Vey lies on the floor, laughing softly. “Strike it, investigator. Then you'll hear my daughter.”
Die Glocke ist kleiner als eine Hand und: The bell is smaller than a hand and heavy as a stone. It hums the lullaby when you move it and stops when you hold still.
Die Glocke ist zerbrochen, die Stimmen s:
The bell is broken, the voices are free. But Vey escaped through the canal, with a new face, I assume.

Someday we'll see her again. I hope we'll recognise her then.

(End of case 5. Talk to Marlowe again.)
Knock the bell off the beam.
Die Hafenwache sagt, es sind nur Betrunk: The harbour watch says they're just drunks.
Agnes Crane sets out the candles.
Die Kreuze stehen bei Namen, die du aus: The crosses are next to names you know from the newspapers: people who died in their sleep. You note the dates.
Die Laternen brennen wieder. Fast. Ich s: The lanterns are burning again. Almost. I still don't sleep well.
The melody breaks off after four bars. It's unfinished, as if someone had been waiting for the missing voices.
Die Münzen, der Mantelfetzen, und Greta: The coins, the scrap of coat, and Greta saw me? ... Okay, okay. Here. There's hardly nothin' in it anyway.
Die Noten bewegen sich, wenn du nicht hi: The notes move when you're not looking. You notice that you're humming along and bite your lip until it stops. Something is written on the last page.
Die Noten hinten summen (gefährlich): Hum the notes in the back (dangerous)
Die Phiolen im Takt der Uhr öffnen, eine: Open the vials in time with the clock, one after another.
The Rust Brothers. Price is right.
Die Schatten in das Silberbad zurückgieß: Pour the shadows back into the silver bath and resilver the mirrors.
Wrap the shard in a cloth.
Die Schränke links öffnen sich nach Rang: The cabinets on the left open by rank. Misfortune files from rank Investigator, the sealed ones from Trusted by the precinct. Rules are rules.
Die Seiten reißen dir die Finger auf, ei: The pages slice your fingers open, one after another, and the blood forms notes. The mist rises into your mouth. Seven voices sing from the book, and it sounds as if they are coming closer.
Die Spiegel zerschlagen, damit er nie wi: Smash the mirrors so he never takes any again.
The music box fits in a child's hand. A moon is painted on the lid, and the brass is shiny where a thumb has touched it a thousand times.
Die Stimmgabel anschlagen und an den Ran: Strike the tuning fork and hold it to the rim.
The cylinder keeps turning by itself. From the tiny box a child sings the next notes, very close to your ear.
Die letzte Seite noch einmal ansehen: Look at the last page again
Die letzte Zelle ist kalt, obwohl der Of: The last cell is cold, although the stove beside it glows.
Die vier Laternen am Brunnen brennen wie: The four lanterns by the fountain are burning again.
Die vier Laternen um den Brunnen. Jeden:
The four lanterns around the fountain. Every evening I light them, every morning they're iced over. In autumn! And my knees can't manage the ladder that often any more.

Take my lighter. Scrape off the frost and get the wicks burning. And look under the hoods. Something isn't right there.
Die? Hat mir der Küster von St. Ebba geb: Those? The sexton of St. Ebba brought them to me, weeks ago. Cried as he did, poor man. For the roof beams, he said.
Dr. Fenwick, Polizeiarzt. Wenn Sie nicht: Dr. Fenwick, police surgeon. If you're not bleeding, keep it short.
Drei Splitter aus dem Krater, aus meinem:
Three shards from the crater, from my cabinet! No broken window, no forced lock. And since then I see lights in the clock tower at the North Gate through my telescope at night. Small, cold lights, like my shards.

I'm too old to climb towers. You aren't.
Drei Splitter in Wachstuch. Zwei sind st: Three shards in oilcloth. Two are silent. The third hums, and something moves inside it when you hold it at an angle.
Drei Töne, dann Stille. Die Walze steht,: Three notes, then silence. The cylinder stops, as if waiting for someone to finish singing the melody.
Du arbeitest langsam, Spiegel für Spiege: You work slowly, mirror by mirror.
Du bist Tilly Brooks. Ich bringe dich na: You're Tilly Brooks. I'm taking you home.
Du drehst den Korken nur einen Spalt. Di: You turn the cork just a crack. The scale breaks off, and the voice speaks.
You carried Hester into the crypt.
Du hast Kinder entführt und Menschen get: You abducted children and killed people.
You hold the lamp to the threads.
You hold the plate against the lamp.
Du klappst den Deckel auf. Die Zeiger st:
You flip open the lid. The hands stand at ten to twelve. Inside is a tiny, faded picture of a woman in a market apron laughing at something outside the frame.

The only dangerous thing about this watch is how sad it makes you.
You're coming with me to Constable Price.
You put both hands on the brass ring.
Du legst einen beschwerten Würfel neben:
You place a weighted die next to his. You both throw. Two sixes. Silas' smile grows thin.

“Very well. What do you want? Money? I have money.”
Du schneidest das Band durch. Tilly reib:
You cut the ribbon. Tilly rubs her wrists. “They drew me every day. My face. Over and over. Until they could do it.”

She holds on to your sleeve until you're back on the street.
Du steckst den Steckbrief ein. Darunter: You pocket the poster. Below it, in Marlowe's handwriting: “Alive. Price wants to see him.”
Du stellst dich zwischen Vey und die Glo:
You place yourself between Vey and the bell under the cloth. It's smaller than you thought, black with soot.

Vey looks at you for a long time. “Then I'll wait for another bell. Kettlegate has many towers.”

The candles go out. When Price storms in, she's gone. But the bell lies in your arms, humming softly.
You brace yourself against the beam.
You wait for the first strike.
Du zählst auf: die Freitagsrunden, die u:
You list it all: the Friday rounds, the knocked-over stalls, the notebook under the barrel. Grimes' face goes blotchy.

“So? You think the precinct cares about a few shillings?”
Dunn beißt auf jede Münze, bevor er sie: Dunn bites every coin before he gives it to you. “You never know.” 35 shillings.
Dunn stempelt den Steckbrief und zählt d: Dunn stamps the poster and counts 25 shillings into your hand. “The lanterns at the Old Market are burning again, sir. My wife thanks you.”
Durch das Summen hörst du etwas Fernes,: Through the humming you hear something distant, answering.
Edmund Thorne sitzt unten. Sein Anwalt h:
Edmund Thorne sits downstairs. His lawyer has three witnesses from Anchor Yard who swear he was there all night. I'm afraid we have the wrong man.

And the file stays open, whether it's closed or not.
Ein Constable mit Bauch und Notizbuch ve: A constable with a belly and a notebook blocks your way. “Market warden Grimes. Whoever wants to sell here pays a stall fee. Whoever snoops around here pays double.”
Ein Hafenarbeiter mit verbundenem Arm si: A dock worker with a bandaged arm sits on a bollard, mending a net with one hand. He doesn't look at you.
Ein Herr mit Medaillen am Revers und ein: A gentleman with medals on his lapel and a vendor's tray full of green bottles spreads his arms. “Dr. Horatio Pratt! My Miracle Tonic cures gout, grief and fear of ghosts. Five shillings a bottle!”
Ein Junge mit zu großer Mütze und einem: A boy with a cap too big for him and a bucket flinches as you approach. “I didn't do nothin'! Whatever it is, it wasn't me!”
Ein Kerl mit Schürze und gebrochener Nas: A fellow with an apron and a broken nose stands by a pit full of sawdust. “Three shillings stake, twelve for the winner. No knives, no precinct magic. Everything else is allowed.”
Ein Kind kam durch den Kohleschacht und: A child came through the coal chute and brought canal water. Miss Wren of St. Brigid sent it.
Ein Korkbrett neben der Treppe, voller S: A cork board by the stairs, full of wanted posters. Most are yellowed and crossed out. Four are fresh, with a red police seal.
Ein Kutscher mit Zylinder und Pferdedeck: A cab driver with a top hat and a horse blanket over his knees touches the brim. “Abel Crouch. Where to?”
Ein Lampenanzünder fällt betrunken in de: A lamplighter falls drunk into the canal, and they send me an investigator. What do you want?
Ein Mann mit tadellosem Halstuch lässt z: A man with an immaculate cravat makes two dice dance over his knuckles. “A little game? Small stake, big luck.”
Ein Mann mit trüben Augen sitzt am Brunn: A man with clouded eyes sits on the edge of the fountain, his hands wrapped in rags. “I don't know your steps. New in town? A penny for a blind man?”
Ein Mann mit weißer Halbmaske und Leders: A man with a white half mask and a leather apron is sanding a plaster face. He doesn't speak. He nods at you and points to a slate beside him.
Ein Mann mit wildem weißem Haar und eine: A man with wild white hair and a dozen lenses on chains spins around. “A visitor! How unusual. Are you here about the star glass? Please say you're here about the star glass.”
Ein Matrose mit Wollmütze flickt ein Net: A sailor in a wool cap mends a net, chewing on a cold pipe. “Tobias Hale. What is it?”
Ein Mädchen in einer viel zu großen Jack: A girl in a jacket far too big for her watches you from a crate. “Nan Kettle. For a penny I know everything.”
Ein Mädchen mit roten Zöpfen und dunklen: A girl with red braids and dark rings under her eyes clutches a doll. “Are you from the police? Nan said you'd come.”
A penny for the veiled woman.
Ein Priester mit Wachsflecken auf der So: A priest with wax stains on his cassock sweeps the chapel steps. “The Lord be with you. He's rarely been with me lately.”
Ein Straßenjunge hat gestohlenes Geld zu: A street urchin returned stolen money.
Ein Wiegenlied, ganz leise. Es ist schön: A lullaby, very soft. It's beautiful. You put the bell away before it gets too beautiful.
Ein alter Mann mit Laterne und Ratsche s: An old man with a lantern and a rattle stamps against the cold. “Tam Pruett, night watch on the canal. What do you want at this hour?”
Ein alter Mann mit einer zerkratzten Anz: An old man with a scratched lighting pole leans against the wall. “Forty years I've lit the lights at the Old Market. And now they freeze under my hands.”
Ein alter Mann mit verbeultem Helm und e: An old man with a dented helmet and a breathing mask around his neck crouches beside a manhole. “You want to go down? Into the old gas tunnels? Nobody goes down there any more. Not since the croaking.”
Ein breiter Mann in einem Mantel aus Ket: A broad man in a coat of chain links stands at the anvil. His skin is grey as a ship's hull. “The inspector. You beat up my sons and put out my fire.”
Ein breiter Mann mit Lederschürze und ve: A broad man in a leather apron with singed eyebrows wipes soot from his hands. “Hugh Brannock. The foundry is closed. For a week now. Family matter.”
Ein breiter Mann zwischen Stapeln von Ta: A broad man among stacks of pocket watches, coats and birdcages. “Bandages, tonic, calming tea. And if you want to get rid of something, I pay fair. Almost.”
Ein breitschultriger Mann starrt aufs Wa: A broad-shouldered man stares at the water. “Looking for work? Go somewhere else. People disappear here.”
Ein dickes Buch mit Messingecken. Jede S: A thick book with brass corners. Every page is a list: name, amount, deadline. Behind some names is a cross in red ink.
Ein dünner Mann mit Ärmelschonern sortie: A thin man with sleeve protectors sorts papers that nobody will ever sign again. “Ambrose Finch, clerk. Twenty-two years with Mr. Thorne. And now this.”
Ein hagerer Herr mit einer Lupe im Auge: A gaunt gentleman with a loupe in his eye wipes dust from a display case. “Antiques, curiosities, heirlooms. All with a history. Some with too much history.”
Ein hagerer Maler mit farbigen Fingern s: A gaunt painter with paint-stained fingers stands at an easel in the fog. “Emil Szabo. Please don't step into the picture.”
Ein hagerer Mann mit Ledersack und Holzf: A gaunt man with a leather sack and a wooden flute steps out of the shadows. Something rustles in the sack. “Jasper Reed, rats and vermin. You're the policeman looking for me?”
Ein hagerer Mann mit Monokel schiebt ein: A gaunt man with a monocle slides a drawer of yellowed papers across the counter. “Formulas. Each only once. The first level I sell to anyone, the higher ones only to people who already walk the pathway.”
Ein hagerer Mann mit langen Armen und Wa: A gaunt man with long arms and cotton wool in his ears leans against the tower door. “WHAT?” He pulls the wool out of one ear. “Oh. What?”
Ein heller, reiner Ton. Für einen Moment: A bright, pure tone. For a moment the world is very clear, and the fog in your head clears.
Ein junger Mann im lila Gehrock lümmelt: A young man in a purple frock coat lounges in his dead uncle's armchair. “Edmund Thorne. If you want to arrest me, be quick about it. I have a hangover.”
Ein junger Mann mit Brille und Arzttasch: A young man with glasses and a doctor's bag yawns. “Owen Pike, medical student. I help out where the doctor is too expensive.”
Ein junger Mann mit Messingknöpfen polie: A young man with brass buttons polishes lenses. He doesn't look up. “Lucan Mews. Assistant. I wasn't at the ball, in case you wanted to ask.”
Ein junges Hausmädchen mit sauberer Schü: A young housemaid in a clean apron curtsies. She smiles a moment too long.
Ein kleiner Mann mit dicker Brille drück: A small man with thick glasses clutches a script to his chest. “Oh! Excuse me. I'm only the prompter. Nobody notices me, that's my job, so to speak.”
A soft breathing, even and deep. Somewhere a child sleeps and dreams of a place where it doesn't have to freeze.
Ein riesiger Mann in einer braun fleckig: A huge man in a brown-stained leather apron looks at you. He waits. He has time.
Ein schwarzer Mann, schwarz vom Kopf bis: A man black from head to boots grins with white teeth. “Ben Sotheby, chimneys and luck. A shilling for a handshake.”
Ein schwarzes Notizbuch mit abgegriffene: A black notebook with worn corners. In the front rehearsal schedules and shopping lists, in the back only notes and always the same name.
Eine Frau im grauen Schleier sitzt an ei:
A woman in a grey veil sits at a dressing table combing a wig. In the mirror her face changes when you blink: Lavinia, Marlowe, someone you don't know.

“Inspector. Sit down. I've worn your face before, did you know that?”
Eine Frau in Grau tritt hinter dem Altar:
A woman in grey steps out from behind the altar. Silver hair, eyes like winter water. Miriam Vey.

“You took a son from me. I had already lost a daughter. Do you know what that's like?”
Eine Frau in Grau, das Haar straff gesch: A woman in grey, hair tightly parted, folds laundry with sharp creases. Her voice is soft and pleasant. “Imogen Wren. I run St. Brigid. The children are asleep, please speak quietly.”
